sources.entry: Live Helper Chat - Live Support chat for your website. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Live Helper Chat is an open-source, PHP-based live support chat application for adding operator-staffed chat to websites.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web application that brings live support chat to a site, with operators handling visitor chats from a back office. It supports multiple operators, departments, chat transfers, canned messages, a chat archive, transcripts (print and email), and a site widget or page-embed mode. Visitor features include prefilled and custom form fields, online user tracking with geo detection, and proactive chat invitations. A bot feature can connect to third-party AI services, and the README lists many integrations such as Jitsi voice/video, a REST API, Telegram, WhatsApp via Twilio, Shopify, LDAP, and SSO. It states that it is used in production handling over 10,000 chats per day. Install is by cloning the repo and running composer install (PHP 8.2 minimum), or by downloading a release.
use_cases: Add live chat support to a company website
Let support operators handle multiple website chats at once
Route visitors to departments or operators by language or geo
Connect an AI or chatbot to website visitor chats
Send chat transcripts to visitors by email
Track operator performance and chat statistics
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the most recent release from the releases section (no composer install needed)
notable: Bot feature that can plug in third-party AI services such as ChatGPT, Ollama, Gemini, and Dialogflow
Stated production use with over 10,000 chats per day
Visitor distribution to operators based on GEO, language, or custom attributes
Desktop clients for Windows, Linux, and Mac
Does not depend on third-party cookies
caveats: Several integrations are marked as paid (e.g. Agora) or depend on extensions with webhooks enabled
Some listed integrations are described as deprecated (ChatGPT Assistant, to be deprecated by OpenAI)
Full-scale features such as ElasticSearch and NodeJS are described for high-load setups, implying extra infrastructure
